title: Navigation API: Enable third-party JavaScript embeds to safely use the navigation API

labels.name: topic: navigation API
labels.description: Topics directly related to the navigation API

body:
> [!NOTE]
> 🤖 **This issue was filed by an AI agent** (Claude, running in the [Pi](https://github.com/badlogic/pi-mono) coding agent) on behalf of @yoavweiss, migrating still-live issues out of [WICG/navigation-api](https://github.com/WICG/navigation-api) before that repository is archived. The migration scope was agreed with @noamr.
>
> This is a **migration of an existing discussion, not a new proposal**. The original author is credited below and the original thread is linked. Filed for triage — cc @noamr.

**Migrated from:** WICG/navigation-api#18 — filed by @colinclerk (2021-02). 17 comments.

---

### The problem

Third-party JS widgets can't safely use the history API on host pages. Writing `history.pushState()` conflicts with the host's router, which typically wraps the History API and has strict expectations about `state`. Concrete example from the original issue: doing this on a Next.js site triggers [`popstate-state-empty`](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/blob/canary/errors/popstate-state-empty.md).

The current workaround is for widget vendors to ask developers to **hand them the host router's `push`/`replace` implementations**, which is fragile, framework-specific, and doesn't compose.

### Why it matters for the navigation API

Widgets want push/replace for real reasons: navigating to a developer-supplied callback URL without a full reload, and giving their own subpages real URLs. The navigation API's `info` and per-entry `state` in principle allow a third party to participate without clobbering host state — the question is whether there's a safe, explicitly-scoped way to expose that.

This is a hard design problem (it edges toward per-party history partitioning), and it saw no movement after 2022. Migrating rather than dropping it because the underlying pain is real and unaddressed, and the ecosystem shape that caused it hasn't changed.

cc @colinclerk @domenic
